assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin physiology to GLP-1 receptor agonists is a rare unbroken line from basic hormone biology to therapies that have transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care, with cardiovascular and renal benefits and emerging neurological interest. Scale of patient impact and clarity of the discovery are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Holst for GLP-1 physiology and the incretin effect, Drucker for GLP-1 biology and the therapeutic concept, Knudsen for the long-acting liraglutide/semaglutide design. Mojsov's contribution to identifying the active GLP-1 peptide is a real credit-allocation problem, and only three can be named.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by large outcome trials and broad clinical adoption over more than a decade; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Fair division of credit among Mojsov, Holst, Drucker and industrial development; my recollection of early peptide work by others outside the list is unverified.
Long-term safety and neuropsychiatric effects of the drugs are still being characterized.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new mode of organelle-to-nucleus signalling and a general principle of proteostasis, with relevance to diabetes, neurodegeneration (including Parkinson's disease) and cancer. Conceptually clean and original.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently dissected the IRE1/HAC1/XBP1 pathway in yeast and mammals, a natural two-person pairing. Other contributors to the pathway are not on the supplied credit list.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism extensively confirmed for over twenty years; the translational link to human disease is more indirect than for therapeutic candidates but still strong.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers fundamental cell biology over a therapy-driven discovery.
Credit for the PERK and ATF6 branches lies outside the named pair.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING explains how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity and links infection, autoimmunity (interferonopathies), cancer immunity and senescence. High originality, a clear mechanism and wide biological reach.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP as the second messenger, which I regard as the decisive step; Barber discovered STING. The other credited names (Sun, Wu, Ishikawa) were key co-authors, so a two-person configuration looks defensible.
assessment.maturity: Independently replicated and structurally characterized; therapeutic translation (STING agonists and antagonists) is still unproven in the clinic, so impact is mostly mechanistic so far.
uncertainties: Ishikawa's early STING contribution relative to Barber may be contested.
Clinical payoff has not yet materialized.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new therapeutic modality, with spreading application to autoimmunity.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed the costimulated CAR design, June the first clinical success in CLL and the clinical platform, and Rosenberg pioneering adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified T-cell trials. The original chimeric receptor concept by others not on the list is an allocation concern.
assessment.maturity: Approved products, years of follow-up and multiple confirmations; solid-tumour success remains limited and safety issues persist.
uncertainties: Omission of the originators of the chimeric receptor concept makes a fair three-person split contentious.
Long-term toxicity such as secondary malignancy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishing long-lived, self-organizing adult stem-cell organoids created a platform for disease modelling, host-pathogen work, drug testing and personalized medicine. The discovery is clear and has transformed experimental practice.
assessment.attribution: Clevers defined the Lgr5 stem cell and the culture concept; Sato executed the original intestinal organoid culture. The pair is clean.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and adopted; clinical utility (for example patient-derived testing in cystic fibrosis) is beginning but not yet standard.
uncertainties: The relative weight of the culture innovation versus the Lgr5 stem cell discovery.
Competing pluripotent-cell organoid work is not credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of activity, and it is now ubiquitous in basic research with early clinical translation (vision restoration). Method-driven but with transformative impact.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin was characterized by Nagel, Hegemann and Bamberg; Deisseroth and Boyden brought it to neurons, and Miesenbock made earlier genetically targeted photoactivation. The six-name credit exceeds three, forcing difficult exclusions, notably Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenbock.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and replicated across thousands of studies. Therapeutic evidence is still limited to a few patients.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit is highly contested, so any three-person selection is partly arbitrary.
Tool-oriented rather than a disease-oriented discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 revealed that cancer can arise from blocked cell death and led to venetoclax, a targeted therapy in CLL and AML. A strong bridge between basic and clinical science.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams cloned and characterized the BCL-2 gene family; Vaux showed BCL-2 inhibits cell death. Strasser is credited but appears a later contributor. Other discoverers and the drug developers are not on the list, which weakens a clean configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with long clinical follow-up of venetoclax.
uncertainties: Priority among the groups that identified the BCL-2 translocation and its anti-apoptotic function is not resolved by the supplied credit.
Whether apoptosis is felt to be already honoured by the 2002 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing produced nusinersen, the first effective disease-modifying treatment for spinal muscular atrophy, changing a fatal infant disease into a treatable one. A neurological therapy with a clear chain from mechanism to patient benefit.
assessment.attribution: Krainer led the splicing mechanism and the antisense target; Bennett led the antisense chemistry and drug development. A compact two-person credit is defensible, though other collaborators exist.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with several years of real-world follow-up; durability data continue to accumulate.
uncertainties: The SMN1 gene discovery is not credited here and may merit separate recognition.
Relative weight of an applied drug-development achievement compared with the underlying science.
